claims.text: The degree of atomic size mismatch controls hardness in high-entropy alloys.
The degree of atomic size mismatch controls strength in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic size mismatch induces lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions caused by atomic size differences act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Atomic size mismatch creates local lattice strains.
Mismatch-induced local strains impede dislocation motion.
Enhanced dislocation pinning increases alloy hardness relative to alloys with lower atomic size mismatch.
Enhanced dislocation pinning increases yield strength relative to alloys with lower atomic size mismatch.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will have higher hardness than the low-mismatch baseline.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will have higher yield strength than the low-mismatch baseline.
Greater atomic size mismatch will produce measurable increases in dislocation density.
Greater atomic size mismatch will produce lattice distortions detectable by microscopy or diffraction.
Minimizing atomic size differences reduces lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism should govern behavior while the alloy remains a stable, disordered, single-phase solid solution.
Phase separation, secondary-phase formation, or substantial recovery or recrystallization may cause mechanisms other than mismatch-induced lattice distortion to dominate hardness and strength.
